outcome: The top card of the library moves to the player's hand, as the draw-step action or as part of an effect or cost.
A multi-card draw is performed as individual single-card draws, each of which can fire its own draw trigger.
A replacement effect that refers to the number of cards drawn modifies the whole instruction before any individual draw happens.
Under a one-draw-per-turn restriction, a multi-card draw is carried out only partially, drawing the first card and no more.
When both players are told to draw, the active player draws first, then the other player.

note: shared team turns option, not used in two-player games

outcome: A player with an empty library can still be offered an optional draw, unless a can't-draw effect applies.
An optional draw offered to another player's empty library can be taken unless that player can't draw.
A player who attempted to draw from an empty library loses the game at the next state-based check.
Moving cards from library to hand without the word draw does not fire draw triggers or draw replacements and does not set up a loss on an empty library.

note: introduces draw replacement effects; sub-rules carry the outcomes

outcome: A draw replacement effect applies even when the library is empty.
A replaced draw within a sequence completes its replacement before the next draw in the sequence.
An additional action on a drawn card is not performed on cards drawn through a replacement of that draw.
The unreplaced parts of the original event occur first, then the resulting card draws happen one at a time.
A card drawn while a spell is being cast stays face down with no characteristics and cannot pay the cost until the spell becomes cast.

note: choice of whether to reveal a card as it is drawn
